missionPremise: Fleet is IN SCOPE as of the operator ruling 2026-09-15 (_decisions/2026-09-15_police_and_fleet_lenses_in_scope.md), which reversed an earlier not-in-the-pilot exclusion because v1 is being retired and an undesigned lens does not keep its current level of service after cutover, it disappears. findings: the Samsara live mapper DOES fall back to a colliding sentinel, three times on one record: recordId to unknown-vehicle, unitLabel to Unnamed unit, status to unknown. CORRECTED MID-LANE: the first version of this finding said Fleet was the only mapper doing that, read off Fleet's mapper and assumed about the others. Measured by running all five: 4 of 5 are exported and EVERY one invents exactly 3 strings on an empty row (unknown-patrol/Unnamed unit/unknown, unknown-apparatus/Unnamed apparatus/unknown, unknown-project/Untitled project/unknown; mapRealCallVolumeRecord is not exported). Samsara and Spireon share the literal "Unnamed unit", so the collision crosses lenses as well as rows. The finding is systemic, not local, and the previous lane reported only the recordId leg.

three refusals are generated-only and do not survive the cutover: operatorRef, operatorBasis and inventoryBasis. The live record carries operator: null with NO basis, which is the absence-with-no-basis defect this program hunts.

two default page sentences become FALSE on a granted feed. renderFleet overwrites #fleet-roster-inventory and #fleet-operator-basis only when extras.inventoryBasis and extras.operators[0] exist, and the live composer returns extras { realStatusCounts } only. So the page says 'The operator dimension has not been read for this pack' about a region that WAS read, and says the inventory position has not been read about a product rule that was never a reading.

assertRecordShape is called by composeDomain and by NOTHING in src/vendor-live.mjs. Run by hand over the mapper's own output it REFUSES with three faults: status outside the declared enum, operatorRef required and absent, odometerBand required and absent. The live record also carries 12 fields the shape does not declare. One fault is a declared position in the module header; the other two are declared nowhere, and the shape table's own preamble claims a fixture and a real record are the same shape.

among those 12 undeclared fields are vin, make, model and odometerMiles, which is the field set of an inventory, arriving on the same cutover that drops the one sentence saying this is not one. The generated record carries a declared odometer BAND for exactly that reason; the live record carries the number.
three of the eight shipped roster columns can only fill from a granted feed and render blank on every row of a generated pack, through the renderer's null-is-blank path.

Fleet is AHEAD of Fire and EMS on the tile axis: renderRegionMetrics already branches on extras.realStatusCounts and renderRealStatusTiles already rebuilds the strip one tile per real value. The rule the Fire and EMS board had to state for a build is already the code here.

OPERATOR_REF_FORMAT and OPERATOR_BASIS are declared identically and INDEPENDENTLY in fleet-vehicles.mjs and patrol-vehicles.mjs, so Fleet and Police share one operator-reference namespace and nothing in the product says whether OPR-01 on each is one person.

sharedConstraint.statement: A DRIVER IS A PERSON. The roster groups on an opaque operator reference under a declared format and the record states in its own basis why the name is absent.
sharedConstraint.treatmentPoliceCanShareInFull: draw the reference as a working dimension, put its declared format in the panel head IN WORDS derived from the product's regex rather than as the literal, carry operatorBasis verbatim as the panel basis, and never render a per-person condition breakdown.
sharedConstraint.divergenceFlaggedRatherThanTaken: the two lenses share one reference namespace and neither can resolve it alone, so this design asserts nothing about cross-lens identity and raises it for a ruling. sharedConstraint.warningForPolice: printing the declared format as the regex literal /^OPR-\d{2}$/ is refused by the product's money gate, because the literal ends in a currency symbol. Derive the sentence from the literal and fail closed.

falsifier: If check.mjs could report a pass on an artboard carrying a driver name, an operator reference outside /^OPR-\d{2}$/, a roster that is not the composer's fourteen in the composer's order, or inventory vocabulary in a column header, the instrument would be worthless and this close would be wrong. Sixteen planted defects covering those and twelve other predicates were all caught, each by a specific expected message rather than by a bare non-zero exit. A second falsifier was pre-registered for the boards themselves: if any board rendered a clipped row while a basis beneath it claimed a full count, the design would be wrong. It did, on the first render, and it was fixed and re-rendered.
contradicted: Three expectations carried into this lane were wrong and are recorded rather than quietly dropped. FIRST, the mission suggested the Fire and EMS finding 'when it reads, these tiles are not these tiles' would apply here as a build rule; it does not, because renderRegionMetrics and renderRealStatusTiles already rebuild the strip from the payload, so Fleet is ahead on that axis and restating it would have been a fourth copy of a board that had already been drawn. SECOND, the expectation that Fleet's grouping dimension would want the small-multiples treatment its closest precedent used; it does not, because the dimension is assigned by a modulo over a severity-ordered plan and any cross tab of it against condition reports the stride, which is measured in source-state.json and deliberately not drawn. THIRD, the expectation that a connected lens would have LESS to say than a blocked one; it has more, and worse: a blocked region states an obstacle, while this one silently drops three refusals and keeps two sentences that become false. FOURTH, and this one was this lane's own error rather than an inherited expectation: the first draft of the sentinel finding claimed Fleet was the only mapper falling to three sentinels on one record. That was read off one mapper and assumed about four others. Running all five refuted it, the board, the folder README and this close were corrected, and the corrected claim is derived from a measurement stored in source-state.json rather than from a reading. It is recorded here because a correction that leaves no trace is how a wrong claim gets re-derived.
